per_window.ps-ns: unresolved: the relaxation study behind the entry (Li and Montelione 1995, doi:10.1021/bi00008a003) is now in the evidence as an abstract only; an extended Lipari-Szabo analysis of 15N R1/R2/NOE at pH 7.1, 30 °C maps sub-nanosecond backbone motion without values (J11, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020145442-r1). The EGFR-ED paper's abstract calls both termini flexible from methyl relaxation (J1, r3).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved: the same abstract reports significant 15N exchange broadening at about 40% of backbone amides, including many at the subdomain interface, read as microsecond interconversion among conformations with partial core-sheet unfolding, hinge bending or disulfide isomerisation as candidate mechanisms; no residue list, rate or population (J12, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020145442-r2).
per_window.slower_than_ms: No judgment: no row gives a conformational rate slower than milliseconds. The pH-dependent interconversion (J2) has no rate, and the film H/D exchange rates (J5) are solvent-exchange rates, kept in undetermined.
per_window.undetermined: Free ligand: pH-dependent interconversion (J2, r2), partial disorder at pH 3.5 and 30 °C versus pH 6.5 (J3, r9), faster amide exchange than mouse EGF at pH 3.5 (J4, r1), film H/D exchange class rates (J5, r10), all unresolved. Bound states, kept apart from the free domain: EGFR-ED-bound methyl mobility (J6, r3), fast-exchange binding (J7, binding kinetics), IDE-bound D10-Q14 helix-to-strand change in 3E50 (J8, r7), EGFR cryo-EM classes 7SZ5/7SZ7 (J9, r12) and complex MD (J10, r13). Not judged: r4 (1MOX receptor dimer packing in an abstract, no ligand motion), r5 (des-Val-Val construct structure, F15-D47 well defined, pH 6.3), r6 (TGF-alpha 8-50 construct structure), r8 (IDE cleavage-fragment mapping, proteolysis not motion), r11 (human EGF homolog film H/D exchange).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Partly: the relaxation study behind the entry, read only as an abstract, says that free mature human TGF-alpha at pH 7.1 ± 0.1 and 30 ± 0.5 °C shows significant 15N exchange broadening at about 40% of its backbone amides, including many at the interface between the N- and C-terminal subdomains, which the authors read as interconversion among multiple conformations on the microsecond timescale; no residue list, rate, population or regime beyond 'microsecond' can be checked, so the verdict stays unresolved and no site or rate can be given. The remaining free-ligand evidence is abstract-level (flexible termini, a pH-dependent interconversion without rate, partial disorder at pH 3.5 and 30 °C).
protein_summary.deposition_readback: None: the input lists no BMRB id and outputs/deposition/HTGFA.json does not exist.
open_conflicts: H/D exchange paper (r10): the prose says TGF-alpha beta-sheet exchange is ten orders of magnitude slower than EGF, while Table 1 gives 1.41 x 10-4 versus 1.88 x 10-3 min-1, about one order. Table values are used.

Conditions of the 1995 relaxation study: the evidence rows (HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020145442-r1, r2) record 'pH neutral' and no temperature, while the cached abstract states pH 7.1 ± 0.1 and 30 ± 0.5 °C; the abstract values are used in J11 and J12.
questions_for_gina: Is the RelaxDB HTGFA set from Li and Montelione 1995 (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003, pH 7.1, 30 °C)? It is the only 15N R1/R2/NOE study of free TGF-alpha found, read as an abstract only; its full text would give the residues with exchange broadening.
Does the pH-dependent conformational interconversion in the 1991 structure paper (r2) show two peak sets at one pH, or a shift between pH values? Only the abstract was readable.
protein_summary.buffer_note: Nine of fifteen rows were read as abstracts, so the free-ligand judgments are unresolved by rule. pH and temperature are part of the state: pH 3.5 at 30 °C and pH 6.5 at 10 or 30 °C are separate states, not one state in exchange; the 1995 relaxation study is at pH 7.1 ± 0.1 and 30 ± 0.5 °C (abstract), buffer unknown. EGFR-, EGFR-ED- and IDE-bound structures are partner-bound states and never enter the wt_apo_answer. The ATR-FTIR data (r10, r11) come from dried films rehydrated with D2O vapour at an unreported temperature and are not comparable with solution NMR. Second reads: no row marked wrong in either case; in the 2026-10-20 re-read Codex left both rows unverified and Claude marked both ok.
